problems.form_value: 'the conversation analysis drew on at most 50 of 70 recorded sessions' ... 'at least 37 dyads (74 people) for the conversation outcome'; agreed-fields entry: '70 audio sessions, 4 excluded for echoes, 16 not included (researcher-only recordings): at most 50 sessions' (confirmed: true)
problems.source_says: Footnote 12 does not say the 16 researcher-only recordings are among the 70 sessions. 70 + 16 = 86, the number of dyads, so the 70 can be the sessions with usable participant audio (66 after the 4 echo exclusions). The conversation REML prints denominator df 50.76. With four fixed-effect terms, the df cannot much exceed the number of dyads minus 4, so it implies about 55 or more dyads, which contradicts 'at most 50'. This is inference, not a printed count. The lower bound of 37 dyads (74 people) still holds under either reading, so criterion 2 is unaffected.
problems.quote: The audio comes from a total of 70 sessions, out of which 4 sessions were excluded from conversation analysis due to prominent echos ... Sixteen recordings were not included in the analysis
problems.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 302), footnote 12; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 304), Sec. 5.1.2, F(1, 50.76) = 6.25

problems.form_value: the REML denominator df (67.03 for ideas, 50.76 for conversation) suggest roughly 70 and 50 dyads
problems.source_says: With an intercept, cue, modality, and their interaction as fixed effects, the denominator df is at most about the number of dyads minus 4. The printed df therefore imply at least about 71 dyads for the idea models and at least about 55 for the conversation model, not about 50. The ideas figure fits 82 dyads (86 minus the 4 dropped sessions) less about 11 dyads with missing covariates, and the conversation figure fits 66 less a similar number.

problems.source_says: Not every analysis is at the dyad level. The homogenization test compares idea-level cosine distances pooled across dyads, and the form itself codes S1-O4 with unit 'output'. The REML models (S1-O1 to S1-O3) and the noticing analysis are at the dyad level. People counts are unaffected.

confirmed: n_randomized = 172 people: 172 participants randomly assigned to the four conditions, in 86 dyads; the conclusion repeats 172 randomly assigned (PDF p. 5, printed p. 300, Sec. 4.1.1; PDF p. 11, printed p. 306, Sec. 8; abstract, PDF p. 2).
counts_are = people is right: gender counts sum to 172 (42 male + 127 female + 3 non-binary); ages 18 to 37, median 21; course credit or $20 for 75 minutes (PDF p. 5, Sec. 4.1.1).

Four sessions dropped (2 for echoes, 2 for technical issues), so at most 82 dyads (164 people) entered any analysis; the abstract's 'N=172 participants in dyads completed' ignores these drops, and the form rightly treats 172 as randomized, not analyzed (PDF p. 5, Sec. 4.1.1; PDF p. 2, abstract).

Thirteen participants without prior design experience and topic knowledge were excluded from analyses that use these factors; the REML models use both as group-level (0/1/2) random effects (PDF p. 5, Sec. 4.1.1; PDF p. 7, Secs. 5.1 and 5.1.1).

No count of people or dyads analyzed is printed for any arm or outcome: not in the text, the Fig. 5 box plots, Figs. 6 and 10, or Appendix A; null per-arm counts and null study-level n_analyzed are correct (PDF pp. 2-21; Fig. 5 on PDF p. 8).

Incidental numbers do not give arm sizes: 578 divergence cues at about 18 per session and 41 transcripts double-coded for cue noticing are not arm counts (PDF p. 11, Sec. 6.3; PDF p. 7, Sec. 4.1.4; PDF p. 5, Sec. 4.1.2).
Idea-outcome lower bound holds: 86 - 4 - 13 = 69 dyads (138 people), consistent with the ideas REML df of 67.03, which needs about 71 dyads (PDF p. 5, Sec. 4.1.1; PDF p. 7, Sec. 5.1.1).

Footnote 12 (70 audio sessions, 4 excluded for echoes, 16 researcher-only recordings) and the 2 sessions excluded from noticing coding are paraphrased faithfully in participants.exclusions (PDF p. 7, footnote 12 and Sec. 4.1.4).

S2 has no human participants: cues were regenerated for the study transcripts (Fig. 9 shows S3, S11, S14), so counts_are = other and null counts are right (PDF p. 11, Sec. 6.3; PDF p. 18, printed p. 313, Fig. 9).
The pilot (N=10 users, 5 dyads) is a separate earlier sample and is not in the 172 (PDF p. 4, printed p. 299, Sec. 3.1).

No shared sample: the paper cites the authors' 2024 C&C study [104] only as prior work; that study (c889 in candidates.json) is a separate Wizard-of-Oz sample of 14 triads, and a web search found no other paper reporting the 172-person experiment (PDF p. 3, printed p. 298, Sec. 1; reference [104]; candidates.json c889).
Population = students is supported: course credit as part of a course requirement, and almost all participants in psychology or cognitive science (PDF p. 5, Sec. 4.1.1; PDF p. 11, Sec. 7).
Criterion 2 holds for S1 alone: at least 138 people (69 dyads) analyzed in the idea outcomes on the most conservative arithmetic, and 172 people randomized (PDF p. 5, Sec. 4.1.1).
summary: The people counts hold: 172 people were randomized in 86 dyads, no analyzed or per-arm count is printed, and at least 69 dyads (138 people) remain in the idea analyses after the four dropped sessions and 13 covariate exclusions, so criterion 2 is met. Details are refuted: the form's 'at most 50 of 70 sessions' for the conversation analysis is not in footnote 12 and conflicts with the printed df of 50.76 (about 55 or more dyads), the open question misreads the df the same way, one sentence wrongly says every analysis is at the dyad level, and the source note wrongly says the markdown stops at reference [77].
